chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Freelancing after Whiteman and working for Nat Shilkret
summary: He wrote for Willard Robinson and Don Voorhees but mostly for Nat Shilkret's radio work for about three years.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: All right, so what did you do after that and let's synopsize this.

Well, I got out of the Whiteman band and I called up Nat or Nat called me up, heard about it and he wanted to know if I'd do some work in the radio and I had been in touch -- I ran into Willard Robinson Rose and he asked me if I would do some things for him and his Deep River orchestra. Bill had still been working with us in the Whiteman band on the radio show, so I don't know what he did, I think he went out to the coast, or he did something else.

Anyway, Willard asked me to do some work for him and I did, so I was sort of free-lancing around, at different places. I did a couple of things, and I also did some work for Don Vorhees and none of this jelled for me because it didn't jell for any of these guys except Nat. And Nat was working you know, he had about five radio -- radio was his bag. So I went to work for
Nat and I worked for him about three years. And the Casa Loma.
